clue.text: Do something unpleasant to whisky King's to consume

parts.note: malt is a single-malt whisky
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A drinker urges the King to down his whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat someone is to treat them badly, a synonym for doing them harm.

clue.text: Pale characters on slab I translated

indicators.note: translated means the letters are turned into a new form, rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone translates an inscription carved on a stone slab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' is the anagram signal for ON SLAB I.
explanation.definitionFit: Albinos lack pigment, so they are pale-skinned people.

clue.text: Some depart here for Epping, as a result

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Travellers are told some trains leave from this station for Epping, on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the T ending 'depart' and finishes with the E opening 'Epping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a consequence, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Planet core's hard to the end

indicators.note: says the hard letter is shifted from its place to the very back of the word

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A geologist remarks that our planet's core is hard right through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' moves the H of HEART from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the planet we live on, one example of a planet.

clue.text: Contest flattering short moves

indicators.note: moves tells us the letters change places

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chess game decided by flattering, brief moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' is the anagram signal for FLATTERING SHORT, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial of strength is a test of power between rivals, a contest.

clue.text: Conservation body involved in genuine hire charge

indicators.note: involved in means the body's letters are wrapped up inside the genuine word

parts.note: real means genuine
NT is the National Trust, Britain's heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A conservation charity is caught up in a real dispute over a hire fee.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the sum paid to hire something, a fee.

clue.text: Umpire in error, dismissing last three? He should show an improvement in quality

definitions.text: He should show an improvement in quality

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire
taken as written

indicators.note: tells us to remove the final three letters of the word error, leaving its start

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire wrongly gives out three batsmen and is told to raise his standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing last three' cuts ROR from ERROR, leaving ER. 'Dismissing' points to cricket, where an umpire gives batsmen out.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner purifies a substance, raising its quality.

clue.text: Carer ultimately involved in new employment as hospital worker

indicators.note: involved in means the picked letter goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting something to use

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the very last letter of the word carer

explanation.surface: A carer ends up in a new job working at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R, the last letter of 'Carer', which goes inside N + USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse looks after patients on the wards, a hospital worker.

clue.text: Fool, for instance, sitting on first-rate pointed weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on puts the earlier pieces above the next one

parts.note: an ass is a fool
EG, exempli gratia, means for instance
A1 (read as AI) means first-rate

explanation.surface: A fool perches on a top-quality spear.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; its digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender spear of southern Africa, a pointed weapon.

clue.text: The sort of seaman that has no leader on board?

indicators.note: says the first letter of the board word is missing

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A ship's crew member who is never in charge of anyone aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no leader' drops the T of TABLE. 'On board' suggests a ship, but 'board' is the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a rank in the Royal Navy, so able describes one sort.

clue.text: Threatened ecosystem: Sun has the news before all others?

indicators.note: before places the news piece ahead of the rest in the word

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
info, information, is news
the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: The Sun newspaper boasts it gets the news ahead of every rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here it is Ra, the sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical forests are endangered habitats, a threatened ecosystem.

clue.text: Brain? One can help with problems!

indicators.note: with problems means the letters are in trouble, jumbled up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever person offers assistance with puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with problems' is the anagram signal for ONE CAN HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: The encephalon is the anatomical name for the brain.

clue.text: Clutch, say, goes when middle part drops out

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: says the inside letters of goes disappear, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A car's clutch fails when its central part falls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when middle part drops out' leaves GS, the first and last letters of 'goes'. 'Say' looks like part of the definition but gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A clutch is a set of eggs laid by a bird at one time.

clue.text: Lucky charm's first to go at racecourse

indicators.note: first to go removes the opening letter of the charm word

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: A punter's lucky charm is the first thing lost at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to go' takes the M off MASCOT. Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, an example of one.

clue.text: A warning cry's something helpful, as previously mentioned

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning cry, with the 's adding S
an aid is something helpful

explanation.surface: Shouting a warning is useful, as was said before.
explanation.walkthrough: Golfers shout 'Fore!' to warn others a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal word for already referred to.

clue.text: Series editor almost restricting one's coverage in restaurants

indicators.note: restricting means the series and editor pieces close round the next piece
almost removes the final letter of the editor word

parts.note: a vetter checks texts, an editor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A series editor nearly limits a writer's restaurant reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts VETTER to VETTE; SER + VETTE then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is a napkin, covering a diner's lap at the table.

clue.text: Professional board rejected chap with record in recent days

indicators.note: rejected means the chap word is sent back the other way

parts.note: a man is a chap
an EP is an extended-play record
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: A professional body turned down a man with a recent conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MAN into NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a sign outside an office showing a professional's name.

clue.text: Excite one over Italy and China?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places one piece above the next

parts.note: an means one
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: A traveller rhapsodises over two countries, Italy and China.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to enliven or stir up, a synonym for excite.

clue.text: The French love shimmering hot African country

parts.note: les is the French plural for the
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: shimmering suggests something wavering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A French lover is drawn to a shimmering hot African land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shimmering' rearranges HOT into THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom in southern Africa, so a country.

clue.text: Conservative rush to express ideology

parts.note: a rush is a reed, a marsh plant

explanation.surface: A Conservative hurries to set out political beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' is a waterside plant, not a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs, a synonym for ideology.

clue.text: Issue almost consumed fellow internally

indicators.note: internally puts the fellow inside the shortened word
almost removes the final letter of the consumed word

parts.note: eaten means consumed
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man nearly gets eaten from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb here; 'almost' trims the final letter and 'internally' sets the fellow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Fool: one taken in by weak politician

indicators.note: taken in by means one piece is held inside the others

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gullible person is duped by a feeble politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts I inside W + MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a feeble, ineffectual person, a fool in the sense of a weakling.

clue.text: Bishop, say, is sweet on Church

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the sweet above the church

parts.note: a pie can be a sweet dish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A bishop has a sweet tooth for food served at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' is a chess piece, not a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the chessmen, an example of a piece.

clue.text: A chicken, processed again put in tin will cause mischief

indicators.note: put in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the tin symbol

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a hen is a chicken

indicators.note: processed means the letters go through a mill and come out rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Processed chicken canned again can only lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges the chicken and 'again' together; 'put in' sets the result inside the chemical symbol for tin. 'A chicken' gives the bird with its article, so 'A' adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenanigans are mischievous goings-on, so the word means mischief.

clue.text: Flower more rapidly losing head

indicators.note: losing head removes the first letter of the speedier word

parts.note: faster means more rapidly

explanation.surface: A flower wilts more quickly once its head is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops F from FASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like garden flower.

clue.text: Restaurant employee evicting one drunk, not spilling a drop!

indicators.note: evicting means throwing out, so a letter is removed from the waiter

parts.note: a waiter serves in a restaurant
I is the Roman numeral one
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A waiter throws out a drunk diner without spilling a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evicting' takes I out of WAITER, leaving WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something watertight lets no liquid leak, a synonym for sealed.

clue.text: Rent? Final instalment of rent needs attention

indicators.note: the final instalment is the closing letter of the word rent

parts.note: an ear means attention, as in lend an ear

explanation.surface: A tenant's last rent payment demands notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent?' is a rip, not money paid for housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a rip in fabric, a synonym for a tear.

clue.text: Brave man holding alien till this time

indicators.note: holding means the brave man wraps round the alien

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A brave man keeps an alien captive until now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' means the hero keeps the film alien captive inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal word meaning up to now.

clue.text: Hurried round animal's lair, being not easily shocked

indicators.note: round means the hurried word goes around the lair

parts.note: hared means ran fast, hurried
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Someone rushed round a fox's den without flinching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurried' is the outer piece and 'round' wraps it about the lair; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hardened is toughened by experience, so unshockable.
